## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: speed limits, slow driving, curves and funeral procession rules
Confusable pairs among the speed limits, curve technique and procession rules, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in trailing lines.

FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A02
The 55 mph figure is both the maximum outside cities and towns and the maximum for school activity buses, while a regular school bus is held to 45 mph. [A02]
Why it matters: group speed limits; difficulty high; confusable bus types.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A02
The default limit inside cities and towns is 35 mph unless posted otherwise, while interstates allow up to 70 mph. [A02]
Why it matters: group speed limits; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A02
Speeding reduces control and raises injury risk, yet driving well under the limit is also linked to more crashes, so the goal is a speed suited to conditions within the posted range. [A02]
Why it matters: group speed choice; misconception target.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A01
The two-second rule governs the gap to the car ahead, while seeing farther ahead is what you need as speed rises, because stopping distance grows [A01] [A02].
Why it matters: group following; confusable gap versus sight distance.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A02
On a curve, the speed reduction happens before the curve, and the speed is then gradually increased through it rather than reduced by braking inside it. [A02]
Why it matters: group curves; misconception target.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A03
On a downhill curve you shift to a lower gear before the descent and start braking earlier than on flat road, not once you are in the bend. [A03]
Why it matters: group curves; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A01
Oncoming drivers may choose to yield to a funeral procession, while drivers going the same way are forbidden to pass it unless there are two or more lanes in its direction. [A01]
Why it matters: group funeral processions; difficulty high; confusable may versus must not.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A01
Procession cars may continue through an intersection behind a lead car that crossed lawfully, while an outside driver facing green must not cut across the procession's path. [A01]
Why it matters: group funeral processions; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-R09 | anchor: A01
Driving on the left is lawful only in situations such as one-way streets and passing, while slower traffic on a multi-lane highway belongs in the far right lane. [A01]
Why it matters: group lane position; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-R10 | anchor: A03
A lane change on a multi-lane road needs a check of the lane beyond your target lane too, because a driver there may be moving into the same space. [A03]
Why it matters: group lane changes; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0056]
